name: Cyprus
headline: Cyprus wrote strong patient controls into its 2019 eHealth law, but the national record those controls govern is not due until 2029.

access.summary: The eHealth law and GDPR give a right to see and copy the record, and the GeSY portal shows prescriptions, referrals, diagnoses and visits. The Commission's 2025 eHealth indicator study scored Cyprus 75% for 2024, against an EU average of 83%.
detail: Section 24 of the Electronic Health Law 59(I)/2019 gives each record holder the right to access and receive their health data electronically, plus all GDPR rights (CyLaw).
The GeSY beneficiary portal shows diagnoses, lab tests, visits, prescriptions, referrals, allergies and vaccinations for people registered with a personal doctor (Offsite, 2023).
The European Commission's 2026 country report says records are reachable through an online portal but the national mobile app is still under development.

The Commission's 2025 eHealth indicator study scored Cyprus 75% for 2024 (EU average 83%). It found 12 of 13 data types available, including imaging reports and late discharge reports; only medical images were missing. No mobile app existed.

control.summary: The GeSY portal shows patients which health professionals viewed their history. Opt-out, data locking and per-provider permissions are in the 2019 law, but they belong to a national record bank that is not yet built.
detail: Section 20 lets anyone object to having an electronic record, and section 24 lets holders set access levels per provider and lock data (CyLaw).
Section 25 says a provider may access the record only with the holder's authorisation, and section 32 requires every access to be logged with date, time and user ID.
Those rights attach to the Single eHealth Records Bank. A 2026 paper calls the eHealth4U system the only prototype of the national record (Digital Health).
In GeSY today, the portal's access log lists GeSY professionals who previewed a patient's history or profile (Ygeia Press, 2023). A way to hide data in GeSY was not verified.

privacy.summary: GDPR and Law 125(I)/2018 apply, and the regulator has acted in health. The state hospital operator OKYpY was fined 46,500 euros over 13 losses of medical files or emergency department records, but fines on public bodies are capped at 200,000 euros.
detail: Law 125(I)/2018 bans processing genetic and biometric data for health and life insurance (section 9) and caps fines on public bodies for non-profit activities at 200,000 euros (section 32) (CyLaw).
The Commissioner's 2024 annual report recorded fines totalling 46,500 euros on OKYpY over 13 incidents of lost medical files or emergency department documents (Dialogos, September 2025).
The eHealth law requires the national record bank to be stored in Cyprus with an encrypted copy at least 20 kilometres away (section 30).

commercial.summary: Genetic and biometric data cannot be used for health or life insurance, and the eHealth law needs each citizen's consent before record data goes into anonymised databases. The same law expects the state to earn revenue from sharing those databases with third parties.
detail: Section 9 of Law 125(I)/2018 prohibits genetic and biometric data processing for health and life insurance (CyLaw).
Section 30 of the eHealth law allows extraction into anonymised databases only with each citizen's consent.
Section 31 sends revenue from supplying anonymised databases to third parties to the state treasury, with part to the eHealth Authority.
No specific Cypriot rules on health data brokers, health advertising or consumer health apps were verified.

journey.summary: GeSY's IT system links personal doctors, referrals, labs, pharmacies, hospitals and claims, and MyHealth@EU patient summaries and e-prescriptions went live in 2025. The integrated national record has a 21.1 million euro budget with full operation planned for December 2029.
detail: The Health Insurance Organisation calls its IT system the backbone of GeSY, linking personal doctors, specialists, labs, pharmacies, hospitals and claims through a provider portal (HIO).
A 2026 paper says the system built for GeSY serves providers and beneficiaries mainly for reimbursement, and a national record remains deficient (Digital Health).
Cyprus activated MyHealth@EU patient summary and e-prescription services in May 2025 and plans lab results, imaging and discharge reports next (National eHealth Authority).
The integrated record (OHFYP) budget is 21.11 million euros over 84 months, with full operation in December 2029 (Politis, September 2026).

clinical.summary: GeSY professionals can preview a patient's GeSY history, and every view is logged. The Commission found public and private hospitals supplying data to the national access service, but a full national record is not yet built.
detail: The portal access log records GeSY professionals who previewed a patient's medical history or profile, which shows clinicians can view it (Ygeia Press, 2023).
The Commission's 2025 study found 8 of 11 provider types supplying data, including public and private hospitals, and noted that doctors can access a citizen's health data (European Commission).
The 2019 law allows provider access only with patient authorisation, but the national bank that would apply this is not operating (CyLaw, Digital Health).
Cross-border lab, imaging and discharge report exchange through MyHealth@EU is a planned second phase (National eHealth Authority).

research.summary: On paper, record data can enter anonymised research databases only with each citizen's consent. That rule applies to a bank not yet built, and no general research opt-out for GeSY data was verified.
detail: Section 30 of the eHealth law requires citizen consent before data leaves the Single Bank for anonymised databases (CyLaw).
The National Bioethics Committee, set up by Law 150(I)/2001, runs ethical review of biomedical research and sets review fees.
Cyprus expects to join HealthData@EU, the EHDS secondary-use network, in 2027 (CBN, April 2026).

ai.summary: Clinical AI is governed by EU device law and the EU AI Act, whose medical device duties now start 2 August 2028. Cyprus has named AI Act authorities, but no national clinical AI rules were verified.
detail: The Commissioner of Communications is Cyprus's AI Act notifying authority, market surveillance authority and single point of contact (European Commission AI Act Service Desk).
Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 moved AI Act duties for AI inside regulated products such as medical devices to 2 August 2028 (Cuatrecasas).
The eHealth Authority president spoke on responsible AI at EHDS-AI Connect 2026 in Limassol in April 2026, which is not binding guidance (CBN).

journeyNote: GeSY links personal doctors, labs, prescriptions and claims, and hospitals supply data to the patient portal. Discharge reports arrive late and medical images are not shared. The integrated national record is due December 2029.

news.headline: EU study places Cyprus below EU average on online record access
news.why: Cypriot patients see less of their record online than most Europeans.
